cards.explanation: The answer is False. John 4:2 says it was not Jesus who baptized, but His disciples. The Pharisees were aware He was gaining and baptizing more disciples than John (John 4:1), yet verse 2 sets it straight. It's like a head baker getting all the credit while the crew works the ovens, friends.

The answer is Samaria, friends. John 4:4 says, “Now He had to pass through Samaria.” Had to. That's the text's own word, and I'm not about to argue with it. Samaria is the region where He meets the woman at the well.

The word is weary, bakers. John 4:6 says Jesus was “…weary from His journey…” so He sat down by the well. Tired is something I understand after a full day of stamping. Nobody pressing cookies all day is skipping to the finish line.

The answer is “Give Me a drink,” friends. When the Samaritan woman comes to draw water, Jesus says to her, “Give Me a drink.” It's a short, plain request. Jesus speaks first, and that's what gets the whole conversation rolling.
The answer is False, bakers. John 4:8 says His disciples had gone into the town to buy food. So when the woman comes to draw water, they're away from the well. Jesus is the one who speaks to her.

The answer is that Jews do not associate with Samaritans, friends. The text adds it in parentheses: “For Jews do not associate with Samaritans.” She says, “You are a Jew…” and she wonders how He can ask her, a Samaritan woman, for a drink. That's what has her so surprised.

The answer is that He has nothing to draw with, bakers. She says, “Sir, You have nothing to draw with and the well is deep.” She's looking at the facts: no bucket, deep well. I bet she was wondering how in the world He'd get any water at all.

The answer is True, friends. In John 4:12 she asks, “Are You greater than our father Jacob, who gave us this well and drank from it himself, as did his sons and his livestock?” She's holding up a big name against a stranger sitting at the well. It's a bold question.

The answer is that they will never thirst, bakers. Jesus says, “…whoever drinks the water I give him will never thirst.” (John 4:14) No refills needed. That's the difference between this water and the well water.

Her reason is so she won't keep coming here to draw, friends. She says, “Sir, give me this water so that I will not get thirsty and have to keep coming here to draw water.” (John 4:15) She wants to stop making the trip. I think anyone who has hauled water, or groceries, knows that feeling.
She replies, “I have no husband,” bakers. Then Jesus tells her, “You are correct to say that you have no husband.” (John 4:17) Her answer is short and true.

The word is prophet, friends. She says, “Sir, I see that You are a prophet.” (John 4:19) Jesus told her about her five husbands, and now she's seeing Him differently. I'd say she's paying close attention.

The answer is False, bakers. She says, “Our fathers worshiped on this mountain, but you Jews say that the place where one must worship is in Jerusalem.” (John 4:20) The mountain and Jerusalem are the two places in question. The question is where to worship.

The answer is on neither one, friends. Jesus says, “a time is coming when you will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem.” (John 4:21) She gave Him two choices, and He said neither. That's a plot twist.

The answer is in spirit and in truth, bakers. Jesus says, “…the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and in truth…” (John 4:23) He also says, “God is Spirit, and His worshipers must worship Him in spirit and in truth.” (John 4:24) It's about how we worship, not where.
The answer is True, friends. Jesus says, “…the Father is seeking such as these to worship Him.” (John 4:23) The Father is the one doing the seeking. I think that's worth a smile.
Jesus answers, “I who speak to you am He,” bakers. (John 4:26) She said the Messiah is coming, and He tells her the One speaking to her is He. A big moment at a well.

The answer is False, friends. John 4:27 says the disciples were surprised He was speaking with a woman. But no one asked Him, “What do You want from her?” or “Why are You talking with her?” Surprised, yet neither question was put to Jesus.

She tells the people, “Come, see a man who told me everything I ever did,” bakers. She goes on, “Could this be the Christ?” (John 4:29) She doesn't hold back. She goes back to the town, and she invites them to see for themselves.
The answer is False, friends. John 4:30 says, “So they left the town and made their way toward Jesus.” They came out to Him. When a neighbor says come see, they came.

They ask one another if someone brought Him food, bakers. The disciples say, “Could someone have brought Him food?” (John 4:33) I think they were still stuck on the plain meaning of food. They had just come back with some from town.

His food is to do the will of the One who sent Him and finish His work, friends. Jesus explains, “My food is to do the will of Him who sent Me and to finish His work.” (John 4:34) The disciples had urged Him, “Rabbi, eat something.” (John 4:31) His answer points to something bigger than a meal.

The answer is True, bakers. Jesus says, “…lift up your eyes and look at the fields, for they are ripe for harvest.” (John 4:35) He says they were already ripe, no more waiting. Ripe fields, right now.

He sent them to reap what they have not worked for, friends. Jesus says, “I sent you to reap what you have not worked for; others have done the hard work, and now you have taken up their labor.” (John 4:38) Others did the hard work. The disciples get to step into it.

The word is testimony, bakers. John 4:39 says many of the Samaritans from that town believed in Jesus because of the woman's testimony. Her words were, “He told me everything I ever did.” She told them what happened, and they believed. A simple story, passed along.

The answer is two, friends. John 4:40 says the Samaritans asked Him to stay with them, and He stayed two days. Remember what the text said earlier: “For Jews do not associate with Samaritans.” (John 4:9) So a Jewish man staying in a Samaritan town is something, and I think it's a big yes.

The answer is the Savior of the world, bakers. They tell the woman, “we have heard for ourselves, and we know that this man truly is the Savior of the world.” (John 4:42) They didn't stop at her words. They heard Him for themselves.
